questions.question: Which feature is not commonly associated with French colonial architecture in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ornate Mughal domes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• French colonial architecture in India is characterized by features such as **wide verandas, tall doors and windows, and sloped tiled roofs**.
 
• The architecture incorporates **European design principles**, emphasizing symmetry, simplicity, and functionality.
 
• **Ornate Mughal domes** are not part of French colonial architecture; these are typically associated with **Mughal architecture**, which has a distinct Indo-Islamic style.
 
• French settlements like Pondicherry showcase **colonial-style buildings painted in pastel hues**, with arched doorways and minimal ornamentation.
 
• French colonial architecture reflects a fusion of European and Tamil influences, but it distinctly avoids the intricate detailing characteristic of Mughal structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **French Colonial Architecture:**

 
 
• Developed during the French colonial period, it is known for its **neoclassical design elements** and open layouts to suit tropical climates.
 
• Key features include **high ceilings**, elevated plinths, and large courtyards to enhance airflow and cooling.
 
• Structures often used **lime plaster and brick masonry**, with minimal decorative elements.
 
• The colonial grid layout of towns like Pondicherry reflects a planned urban design approach.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Originating in the 16th century, Mughal architecture is known for its **ornate domes, intricate carvings, and use of marble.**
 
• Key monuments include the Taj Mahal, Humayun’s Tomb, and Jama Masjid.
 
• It blends Persian, Indian, and Islamic styles, emphasizing symmetry and elaborate ornamentation.
 
 
 
• **European Colonial Influence in India:**
 
 
• European colonial powers like the French, British, and Portuguese left distinct architectural legacies in India.
 
• The British introduced **Victorian Gothic and Indo-Saracenic styles**, while the Portuguese favored baroque designs.
 
• French colonial architecture is primarily seen in **southern Indian settlements like Pondicherry and Karaikal.**
 
 
 
• **Colonial Urban Planning:**
 
 
• French colonies were planned with **grid layouts**, emphasizing organization and efficiency.
 
• Public spaces, churches, and administrative buildings were central to the design.
 
• The legacy of colonial urban planning is still evident in cities like Pondicherry, which retain their heritage charm.

questions.question: Intitally, when the 'Constitution of India' was adopted on 26th November 1949, how many Articles and Schedules did it originally contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**395 Articles and 8 Schedules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• Originally, the Constitution contained **395 Articles** divided into 22 parts and **8 Schedules**.
 
• It is regarded as the **longest written Constitution** of any sovereign nation in the world.
 
• The original Constitution was drafted by the **Drafting Committee**, headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Chairman of the Committee.
 
• Over time, the Constitution has undergone several amendments, increasing the number of Articles and Schedules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles:** The Constitution originally contained 395 Articles addressing different aspects such as Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, Union and State relations, etc.
 
• **Schedules:** The 8 Schedules at the time of adoption dealt with subjects like allocation of powers between Union and States, provisions related to Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes, and administration of tribal areas.
 
• **Amendments:** As of now, the Constitution has been amended multiple times, with changes such as the addition of new parts, Articles, and Schedules. Currently, there are 448 Articles and 12 Schedules.
 
• **Directive Principles:** The Constitution incorporates Directive Principles of State Policy inspired by Ireland, aiming to establish a welfare state.
 
• **Constitutional Framework:** It draws inspiration from various global sources including the British parliamentary system, American Bill of Rights, and Australian federal structure.

questions.question: 'The provision for 'Oath or Affirmation' by members of the legislature is mentioned in which Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions related to **Oaths or Affirmations** for various constitutional offices.
 
• It specifies the text of oaths or affirmations to be taken by **Members of Parliament (MPs), Members of State Legislatures (MLAs/MLCs), Ministers, Judges, and other dignitaries**.
 
• The objective of the oath is to ensure that the office bearers uphold the Constitution and perform their duties with integrity and loyalty.
 
• The oath is administered by the **President of India, Governor, or designated authority**, depending on the office.
 
• The Third Schedule demonstrates the significance of constitutional commitment for those holding public offices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oath or Affirmation:**

 
 
• An oath is a solemn promise, often invoking a divine witness, regarding one's future actions or behavior.
 
• An affirmation is a solemn declaration allowed for individuals who do not wish to swear by a deity.
 
• Both forms are recognized under the Indian Constitution and carry equal legal weight.
 
 
 
• **Schedules in the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution originally had 8 Schedules; currently, it has 12.
 
• Each Schedule contains specific provisions related to governance, administration, and federal structure.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Schedules:**
 
 
• **Second Schedule:** Provisions related to salaries, allowances, and privileges of constitutional office holders.
 
• **Fourth Schedule:** Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and union territories.
 
• **Fifth Schedule:** Administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Administration of Oath:**
 
 
• The President of India administers the oath to the Prime Minister, other Union Ministers, and Governors.
 
• In states, the Governor administers the oath to Chief Ministers and other state ministers.

questions.question:
Match the columns: 

 
 

 Column A (Cropping Season)
 Column B (Major Crops - Shuffled)
 
 

 A. Kharif (June-September)
 1. Vegetables, Fruits, Fodder
 
 

 B. Rabi (October-March)
 2. Rice, Cotton, Bajra, Maize, Jowar, Tur
 
 

 C. Zaid (April-June)
 3. Wheat, Gram, Rapeseeds and Mustard, Barley
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A-2, B-3, C-1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kharif crops** (A-2): These are sown in the rainy season (June-September). Examples include rice, cotton, bajra, maize, jowar, and tur.
 
• **Rabi crops** (B-3): These are sown in the winter season (October-March). Examples include wheat, gram, rapeseeds, mustard, and barley.
 
• **Zaid crops** (C-1): These are grown in the summer season (April-June). Examples include vegetables, fruits, and fodder.
 
• The classification of crops based on the cropping season is essential for ensuring efficient agricultural production and resource management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crop Seasons in India**

 
 
• India follows three main cropping seasons: Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid.
 
• Kharif crops are sown with the onset of monsoon and harvested before the winter season.
 
• Rabi crops are sown after the monsoon and harvested in the spring.
 
• Zaid crops are grown between the Kharif and Rabi seasons, typically requiring short durations.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Crop Growth**
 
 
• Temperature, rainfall, and soil type play a crucial role in determining the cropping season.
 
• Kharif crops require high temperatures and abundant rainfall.
 
• Rabi crops grow better in cooler climates and require less water.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Crop Rotation**
 
 
• Crop rotation helps optimize soil nutrients and minimize pests and diseases.
 
• Farmers often rotate Kharif crops like rice with Rabi crops like wheat or mustard.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Cropping Seasons**
 
 
• Understanding cropping seasons helps in planning irrigation and fertilizer usage.
 
• It also aids in maximizing agricultural yield and maintaining food security.

questions.question:
With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1892, consider the following statements and choose the correct option:

1. It significantly increased the number of official members in the Central Legislative Council.

2. It empowered the legislative councils to discuss the budget and address questions to the executive.

3. It introduced the principle of direct election for non-official members of provincial legislative councils.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) 2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Councils Act, 1892, marked a modest but significant step in the evolution of legislative governance in India.
 
• The Act empowered legislative councils to discuss the budget and pose questions to the executive, enhancing legislative oversight and accountability.
 
• It did not introduce the principle of direct elections; instead, it allowed local bodies to recommend members, which were ultimately nominated by the government.
 
• While there was an increase in the number of non-official members in the councils, the Act did not substantially increase the number of official members in the Central Legislative Council.
 
• The Act was a precursor to further reforms, such as those introduced by the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1861:** This Act introduced legislative councils in provinces such as Bengal, Bombay, and Madras, marking the beginning of legislative decentralization in India.
 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms):** This Act introduced the principle of separate electorates for Muslims, a significant development in Indian politics.
 
• **Budget Discussions:** Before the 1892 Act, there was no provision for discussing the budget in legislative councils. The Act allowed members to express their views on financial matters for the first time.
 
• **Unorganized Voting System:** The Act permitted local bodies like municipalities and district boards to recommend members to the councils, but this was far from a direct election system.
 
• **Limitations of the Act:** Despite its progressive features, the Act retained the dominant role of the British government in decision-making and limited the autonomy of Indian representatives.

questions.question: What does 'repo rate' refer to in India's monetary policy?

options.text: Rate at which the government borrows from banks
Rate at which consumers take loans
Rate at which commercial banks borrow from the RBI

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rate at which commercial banks borrow from the RBI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The repo rate is the interest rate at which the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** lends short-term funds to commercial banks in India.
 
• It is a key monetary policy tool used by the RBI to regulate liquidity, control inflation, and stabilize the economy.
 
• A higher repo rate makes borrowing costlier for banks, which in turn increases loan rates for consumers, thereby controlling inflation.
 
• A reduction in the repo rate makes borrowing cheaper for banks, encouraging lending and investment, which boosts economic growth.
 
• The repo rate is reviewed bi-monthly during the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meetings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reverse Repo Rate:**

 
 
• It is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks.
 
• A higher reverse repo rate encourages banks to park their funds with the RBI, reducing liquidity in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):**
 
 
• The CRR is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained as reserves with the RBI.
 
• A higher CRR reduces liquidity, while a lower CRR increases funds available for lending.
 
 
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):**
 
 
• This is the percentage of net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that banks must hold in the form of liquid assets like cash, gold, or government-approved securities.
 
• SLR is used to regulate credit growth and maintain financial stability.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• It is a six-member committee constituted by the RBI to set the repo rate and other monetary policy instruments.
 
• The MPC aims to achieve inflation targeting while fostering growth in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Repo Rate Changes:**
 
 
• An increase in the repo rate leads to higher interest rates on loans and deposits, helping to control inflation.
 
• A decrease in the repo rate encourages borrowing and investment, boosting economic activity.

questions.question: What is a unique feature of the AstroSat mission operated by ISRO?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Simultaneous multi-wavelength observations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• AstroSat is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory, launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on **28 September 2015**.
 
• A unique feature of AstroSat is its ability to perform **simultaneous observations across multiple wavelengths**, including visible light, ultraviolet, and X-rays.
 
• It carries five scientific payloads that work together to provide data in different parts of the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• AstroSat's multi-wavelength capability allows it to study high-energy processes in the universe, such as neutron stars, black holes, and active galactic nuclei, with unprecedented detail.
 
• It is comparable to some of the world's leading space observatories, like NASA's Hubble Space Telescope and Chandra X-ray Observatory, in its ability to study celestial objects comprehensively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multi-Wavelength Astronomy:**

 
 
• It involves observing celestial objects across different parts of the electromagnetic spectrum, such as visible, infrared, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays.
 
• This technique helps uncover diverse physical processes occurring in astronomical phenomena that might not be visible in a single wavelength.
 
 
 
• **AstroSat's Payloads:**
 
 
• UVIT (Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope): Captures data in near-ultraviolet, far-ultraviolet, and visible light.
 
• SXT (Soft X-ray Telescope): Observes soft X-rays to study high-energy sources.
 
• LAXPC (Large Area X-ray Proportional Counter): Focuses on hard X-rays for studying compact objects like neutron stars and black holes.
 
• CZTI (Cadmium Zinc Telluride Imager): Detects hard X-rays and studies gamma-ray bursts.
 
• SSM (Scanning Sky Monitor): Monitors the sky for transient X-ray sources.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Contributions:**
 
 
• AstroSat has provided insights into star formation, galaxy evolution, and the behavior of cosmic phenomena like black holes and pulsars.
 
• It has observed rare cosmic events such as tidal disruption events and gamma-ray bursts.
 
 
 
• **Global Collaboration:**
 
 
• AstroSat data is shared with the international scientific community, fostering collaboration and advancing global astrophysical research.

questions.question:
Consider the following two statements, labeled Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Evaluate them and choose the appropriate answer from the given options.

Assertion (A): The standard distance between the penalty spot and the goal line on a football field is 11 meters.

Reason (R): This distance allows the goalkeeper a fair reaction time while challenging the accuracy and confidence of the penalty taker.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The penalty spot in football is positioned **11 meters (12 yards)** from the goal line as per the Laws of the Game set by FIFA.
 
• This distance was formalized in 1891 when the penalty kick rule was introduced to ensure fairness and maintain a balance between the penalty taker and the goalkeeper.
 
• The reasoning behind the distance is to provide the goalkeeper with a fair reaction time while simultaneously challenging the accuracy and confidence of the penalty taker.
 
• The penalty kick is a direct free kick, and only the penalty taker and the goalkeeper are allowed to be in the penalty area during the kick.
 
• The goalkeeper must remain on the goal line until the penalty is taken but may move laterally to prepare for the shot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Penalty Kick Overview:**

 
 
• Introduced in 1891 as a measure to prevent intentional fouls near the goal.
 
• A penalty kick is awarded when a player commits a direct free kick offense inside their own penalty area.
 
• The penalty spot is a fixed point from which the penalty taker must shoot the ball.
 
 
 
• **FIFA Laws of the Game:**
 
 
• The Laws of the Game are maintained by the International Football Association Board (IFAB), with FIFA as a key member.
 
• These laws dictate the dimensions and markings on the football field, including the penalty area and spot.
 
 
 
• **Goalkeeper Rules During a Penalty:**
 
 
• The goalkeeper must have at least part of one foot touching, or in line with, the goal line until the ball is kicked.
 
• Moving forward off the goal line before the penalty is taken results in a retake if a goal is not scored.
 
 
 
• **Psychological Aspects of Penalty Kicks:**
 
 
• Penalty kicks test the mental focus and composure of both the penalty taker and the goalkeeper.
 
• Studies show that penalty shootouts are often influenced by psychological pressure and confidence.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The penalty kick was first used in a competitive match in 1891 during an Irish Cup semi-final.
 
• It has since become a crucial part of football, used to resolve matches tied after extra time in knockout tournaments.

questions.question:
Which of the following accurately describes The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida, winner of the 2022 Booker Prize?

1.The novel is set during the civil war in Sri Lanka and explores the afterlife of a photojournalist.

2.It is a non-fictional account of archaeological excavations in the Gandhara region.

3. The author, Shehan Karunatilaka, uses satire and ghosts to comment on violence, memory, and political trauma.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida** is a novel by Sri Lankan author Shehan Karunatilaka, which won the **2022 Booker Prize**.
 
• The novel is set against the backdrop of the **Sri Lankan Civil War** and follows the story of a deceased photojournalist navigating the afterlife to uncover the truth behind his death.
 
• Shehan Karunatilaka uses **satire, humor, and supernatural elements**, including ghosts, to explore themes such as violence, memory, and political trauma.
 
• The narrative critiques the **political and social turmoil in Sri Lanka**, highlighting the struggles of individuals caught in the conflict.
 
• Option 1 (civil war and afterlife) and Option 3 (satire and political commentary) are accurate descriptions of the book, while Option 2 (archaeological excavations) is unrelated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Booker Prize:**

 
 
• One of the most prestigious literary awards in the world, it recognizes the best novel written in English and published in the UK or Ireland.
 
• Established in 1969, it celebrates outstanding literary works that contribute to global literature.
 
 
 
• **Sri Lankan Civil War:**
 
 
• A 26-year-long conflict (1983–2009) between the Sri Lankan government and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), seeking an independent Tamil state.
 
• The war caused immense suffering, loss of life, and displacement, heavily influencing Sri Lankan art and literature.
 
 
 
• **Shehan Karunatilaka:**
 
 
• An acclaimed Sri Lankan author whose works often explore themes of history, politics, and identity.
 
• His debut novel, "Chinaman: The Legend of Pradeep Mathew," won several awards, including the Commonwealth Book Prize.
 
 
 
• **Supernatural Elements in Literature:**
 
 
• Ghosts, spirits, and the afterlife are often used to address unresolved conflicts, memories, and traumas.
 
• In "The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida," the supernatural serves as a narrative tool to explore both personal and societal issues.
